Why this theme matters

This theme page collects 6 English passages that touch authenticity as a philosophical concern—whether as a concept to define, a value to pursue, or a problem to examine.

Frequently asked questions

What did philosophers say about authenticity?

They approached authenticity from ethics, metaphysics, politics, and lived practice. The passages below show several of those angles in compact form.

Where can I find philosophy quotes about authenticity?

This archive page is organized for that search intent: verified English quotations, with links to thinkers and related themes.

How should I read these quotations?

Read the sentence first, then check school and source. A quotation is a doorway into an argument, not a substitute for the surrounding text.

  1. How one becomes what one is.
    Friedrich Nietzsche
    Philosophy of Life
  2. Despair is the sickness unto death — the self's refusal to be itself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Proto-Existentialism
  3. Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Transcendentalism
  4. The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.
    Henry David Thoreau
    Transcendentalism
  5. A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Transcendentalism
  6. Despair is not to will to be oneself — or else to will to be oneself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Proto-Existentialism
